title: In vivo genome-wide CRISPR screens of human T cells in solid tumours.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the Springer supplementary zip's member tables by byte-range request. Supplementary Table 2 (IFN-gamma effector screen) opened fully: 19,113 unique gene rows, 0 missing log fold changes (LFC), LFC range -0.878 to +0.993, and 154,882 guide-RNA rows with 0 duplicate guide IDs. Guides per gene: 8 for 18,736 genes, plus one control pseudo-gene 'NTCTRL' holding 2,000 non-targeting guides. Supplementary Table 1 (abundance screen, 58 MB, over the 50 MB cap) read partially by inflating the first 19 MB: its 7 sheet names are Tumor-vs-Input, Spleen-vs-Input and Tumor-vs-Spleen (gene and guide summaries each) plus a dropout-excluded sheet; its Tumor-vs-Input gene sheet is 19,114 rows x 15 columns and its guide sheet 154,883 rows. I computed split-half reliability myself from the guide-level LFCs: Tumor-vs-Input Pearson 0.465 / Spearman 0.315 (Spearman-Brown corrected to 8 guides ~0.64); IFN-gamma effector screen Pearson 0.051 / Spearman 0.040 (corrected ~0.10). Also downloaded and opened the GEO series GSE330227 FPKM table (19,869 genes x 30 samples) and supplementary source-data files MOESM5-MOESM14, which are small per-figure tables (4-10 mice per group).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Library identity (Brunello, ~75,000 guides), two human T cell donors, 22 NSG mice, ~600x library coverage at injection and >1000x at harvest, use of MAGeCK for analysis, and the named top hits P2RY8 and GNAS. Read from the open-access preprint version PMC12485727 (bioRxiv 2025.09.23.678127, CC BY-NC-ND); the Nature article itself is subscription-only. I did not verify the Tumor-vs-Spleen sheets' contents or reliability, nor the gene names in Supplementary Table 1 (its shared-strings block sits past the 50 MB download cap).

a1_downloadable.note: Supplementary zip and all .xlsx files fetched openly from Springer with no login; GEO GSE330227 FPKM table downloaded. The Nature article text is paywalled but the data is not.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Label is already a column: 'neg|lfc'/'pos|lfc' per gene and 'LFC' per guide, in MAGeCK standard output. Verified in the opened files, not inferred.

a3_inputs_present.note: Guide IDs embed the 20-nucleotide protospacer sequence. Gene-level modelling needs features from one bulk UniProt/DepMap download, not thousands of lookups.

a4_units_stated.note: LFC is log2 fold change of normalised read counts (MAGeCK convention). Column names verified in files; no in-file legend states the units explicitly.

a5_enough_rows.note: 19,113 labelled genes per comparison, four genome-wide comparisons, 154,882 guide rows. Counted directly in the files.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Gene tables are tiny; the biggest sheet inflates to ~95 MB of XML and streams fine. Parsing and the reliability analysis ran in under two minutes here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 154,882 guide rows = 2 x 77,441, consistent with the paper's two donors merged over the ~75,000-guide Brunello library; 19,113 genes matches Brunello's ~19,114.

a8_label_provenance.note: Label traces to a physical measurement: counts of guide sequences in DNA sequencing of sorted cells, aggregated by MAGeCK. Not another model's output, not computed from the features.

B1.why: Two spreadsheets, 11 sheets, clean gene-symbol key that joins; not one table. Seen in files.

B2.why: xlsx parse cleanly, but Table 1 sits inside a 95 MB zip as a 58 MB member needing ranged extraction.

B3.why: All four comparisons from one MAGeCK run, one library, same donors; already normalised by the authors.

B4.why: No missing LFCs in Table 2, but count fields are slash-joined strings and stray huge values appeared in Table 1 parsing.

B5.why: Each guide appears twice (154,882 = 2 x 77,441), one variant with a trailing underscore; easy to dedupe, verified in files.

B6.why: MAGeCK-standard column names, documented by MAGeCK but with no legend inside the files themselves.

C1.why: Framed as 'how much in vivo tumour effect is predictable above the measured noise ceiling', it is informative either way.

C2.why: GenePert and the 2026 community T-cell perturbation challenge are open and honestly benchmarked, but on different readouts/species.

C3.why: Novel data nobody has modelled, but the novel readout is ~90% noise by my own split-half measurement.

C4.why: The screen cost 22 NSG mice, two donors and months; prioritising which knockouts to test is genuinely expensive.

C5.why: Dummy global mean, a DepMap-essentiality one-feature baseline, and GenePert all runnable as published comparisons.

D1.why: ESM-2, an open-weight protein language model, matches 19,113 human protein-coding genes directly.

D2.why: 19,113 proteins embedded once on CPU and cached; a gradient-boosted head then trains in minutes.

D3.why: ESM-2 is MIT licensed. Note separately: the screen tables sit under a subscription Nature article, so redistribution is restricted.

E1.why: Hold out whole gene-identity clusters or paralogue families; gene symbol column verified present in files.

E2.why: Thousands of protein families and 23 chromosomes available as held-out groups across 19,113 genes.

E3.why: Global mean and per-chromosome mean are trivial; DepMap mean gene effect is an obvious stronger dummy.

E4.why: I measured it: 8 guides per gene give split-half Pearson 0.465 (abundance) and 0.051 (effector screen).

E5.why: Paper's own Fig. 2b names ZC3H12A, SOCS1, TNFAIP3, MAP4K1 and PTGER4 as must-recover hits; core-essential genes must drop out.

E6.why: 2,000 non-targeting control guides sit in the file as pseudo-gene NTCTRL (verified), plus label shuffling.

E7.why: Public human T-cell screens (Shifrut 2018, Legut 2022, Schmidt 2022) and DepMap join on gene symbol.

E8.why: Guide-level control and treatment counts are in the file, so the paper's MAGeCK gene ranking can be reproduced.

G1.why: Gene symbols only, no Ensembl or UniProt IDs; symbols like LOC113230 and H2AFB3 need resolution. Seen in files.

G2.why: DepMap gene effect and three public human T-cell CRISPR screens are specific partners joinable on gene symbol.

G3.why: One row per gene on both sides; a clean one-to-one join after symbol harmonisation.

G4.why: Asks whether tumour-context T-cell fitness is separable from general cell fitness, which neither dataset answers alone.

H1.why: Genome-wide, both directions of effect reported for every gene, plus 2,000 non-targeting controls. Verified in files.

H2.why: Two donors, one engineered A375 melanoma line, one immunodeficient NSG mouse strain, one guide library.

H3.why: The honest claim can be written precisely, including which readout is excluded because it is noise.

H4.why: Preprint states donor count, mouse count, coverage and the artificial CD3-scFv tumour model explicitly.

I1.why: Marson and Carnevale labs at UCSF/Gladstone, plus CAR-T engineering groups choosing in vivo knockout candidates.

I2.why: A ranked list would redirect which edits get tested, but the measured noise ceiling limits how much it can move.

I3.why: Precision among the top 100 predictions is exactly the decision: which genes go into the next mouse experiment.

I4.why: A DepMap-essentiality lookup plus known T-cell regulator lists likely does much of the work already.

J1.why: Frozen-backbone embeddings, grouped splits, noise-ceiling-aware evaluation and a transfer question: real modelling.

J2.why: Named positive controls (ZC3H12A, SOCS1, CBLB, RASA2) make a nonsense result immediately visible.

J3.why: The noise-ceiling measurement alone is shareable and already produced during this evaluation.

J4.why: No time budget stated anywhere; would need to be set before starting.

J5.why: No kill date written down for this candidate.

existing_models.name: Cancer Immunotherapy Data Science Grand Challenge models (Broad/Eric and Wendy Schmidt Center community benchmark)
existing_models.score_and_split: Over 20 algorithms benchmarked on single-cell Perturb-seq (pooled CRISPR screening read out by single-cell RNA sequencing) covering 73 expert-chosen gene knockouts in mouse T cells transferred into a melanoma model; held-out perturbations, with prospective wet-lab validation of top nominations (Ndufv2, Dimt1). Code at github.com/uhlerlab/cancer_immunotherapy_data_science_challenge.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: They report that performance was driven mainly by which prior data supplied the gene feature representation, with features derived from other perturbation experiments working best; generalising without such prior perturbation data is the open part.

existing_models.name: GenePert (regularised regression on GenePT gene text embeddings)
existing_models.score_and_split: Benchmarked on eight CRISPR perturbation screens across cell types against five pretrained gene embedding models, reporting Pearson correlation and mean squared error on held-out perturbations; preprint reports it beating the compared state-of-the-art methods.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Transfer to perturbations and cell contexts unlike those in the training screens.

existing_models.name: PerturbNet (deep generative model of cell state under unseen perturbations, Molecular Systems Biology)
existing_models.score_and_split: Predicts single-cell expression distributions after unseen chemical or genetic perturbations, using gene functional annotations for CRISPR activation/interference; evaluated on held-out perturbations.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Predicting perturbations with no annotation or chemical-structure analogue in training.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (esm2_t33_650M_UR50D), a protein language model, with a gradient-boosted head on cached embeddings
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU, 16 GB RAM; embeddings computed once for 19,113 human proteins and cached
backbone.licence: MIT (ESM-2). The screen tables themselves come from a subscription Nature article, so redistribution of the data is restricted.

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap CRISPR gene effect across ~1,100 cancer cell lines, plus three public human T-cell CRISPR screens (Shifrut 2018 Cell, Legut 2022 Nature, Schmidt 2022 Science)
integration.join_key: HGNC gene symbol (resolvable to Ensembl gene ID)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Is a gene's effect on human T-cell survival inside a solid tumour just its general effect on cell fitness, or is there a tumour-microenvironment-specific component that cell-line and culture-dish screens cannot see?

controls.positive_control: The model and pipeline must rank the paper's own named true positives (ZC3H12A/Regnase-1, SOCS1, TNFAIP3, MAP4K1/HPK1, PTGER4) in the enriched tail, and core-essential ribosomal and proteasome genes in the depleted tail.
controls.negative_control: 2,000 non-targeting control guides are physically present in the file as pseudo-gene NTCTRL (verified; guide-level standard deviation 0.275), giving a real null distribution; plus label shuffling, which must collapse performance to the dummy baseline.
controls.external_validation: Public human T-cell CRISPR screens (Shifrut 2018, Legut 2022, Schmidt 2022) and DepMap gene effect, joined on gene symbol: train on culture-dish screens, test on this in vivo tumour screen.

honest_claim_h3: Among the 19,113 protein-coding genes in the Brunello guide library, the model ranks how strongly knocking out each gene changes human T-cell abundance inside one engineered A375 melanoma model in immunodeficient NSG mice, using T cells from two donors; it does not speak to patients, and it cannot address the IFN-gamma effector readout, whose gene-level scores I measured to be roughly 90% noise.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use what is known about each human gene to predict whether switching it off helps T cells survive inside a tumour.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per human gene: 19,113 genes, each carrying eight CRISPR guide-RNA measurements, with features built from the protein sequence and from public screens. All counts verified by opening the files.
plain_idea.predict: A log2 fold change: how much more or less common a gene's knockout T cells became inside the tumour compared with the injected pool, measured by counting guide-RNA sequences in DNA sequencing of recovered cells.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Labs engineering CAR-T cells can only test a handful of knockouts in mice, at great cost, so a trustworthy ranked list would redirect that choice. Even if the model fails, the field gets a measured noise ceiling for in vivo T-cell screens.

more_or_better_data.why: The 2026 community challenge trained on 73 gene knockouts in mouse T cells; this dataset has 19,113 human genes, each with 8 guide measurements, from T cells inside a human-relevant solid tumour. Breadth and species both favour us, though their single-cell readout is deeper per gene.

confidence_score.why: Eight guides per gene plus 2,000 non-targeting control guides let us attach a per-gene standard error and flag unreliable genes. I used exactly this structure to measure reliability (0.47 abundance, 0.05 effector); neither GenePert nor the challenge models report calibrated per-gene uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: GenePert (2024) is a regularised regression on frozen text embeddings and is cheap to improve on. But the 2026 community challenge benchmarked 20+ algorithms on held-out perturbations with prospective wet-lab validation, which is a recent and honest evaluation.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The existing models predict single-cell state in mouse T cells, not a scalar log fold change in human cells, so they cannot be run as our baseline on our label with our split. The readout, species and evaluation all differ; three of the four conditions fail.

label_elsewhere.sources: DepMap CRISPR gene effect (known resource, not re-counted this session); public human T-cell CRISPR screens from Shifrut 2018 (Cell), Legut 2022 (Nature), Schmidt 2022 (Science) and Belk 2022 (Cancer Cell), all found by search this session; Open Targets for gene-disease evidence.
label_elsewhere.join_key: HGNC gene symbol (resolvable to Ensembl gene ID)
label_elsewhere.why: Knockout fitness effects are already measured genome-wide for the same gene universe in other contexts, so there is both far more training data and a ready-made external test of whether a model trained in the dish transfers to a live tumour.

risks: Paralogues and members of the same protein complex land in both train and test with near-identical effects, inflating correlation without any real generalisation.
Each guide appears twice in the file (154,882 rows = 2 x 77,441), so any random guide-level split puts the same protospacer sequence on both sides.
Features taken from DepMap or other public screens could include the very screens used to define the label if the compendium is assembled carelessly.
Guide-level technical properties such as GC content and starting abundance correlate with log fold change and can masquerade as biology.
Gene-level scores pool two donors, so donor-specific batch effects are baked into the single label and cannot be split out.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole gene-identity clusters: cluster the 19,113 proteins at 30% sequence identity with MMseqs2 (or group by Pfam family) and keep entire clusters in test. Deduplicate the 2x guide rows by protospacer before any guide-level work. The gene symbol column is present in the files (verified); the cluster column is not and must be built from UniProt/Pfam.
checks: Shuffle gene labels and confirm held-out Spearman collapses to zero.
Compare every reported number against the measured split-half ceiling (Spearman 0.315 for Tumor-vs-Input, 0.040 for the effector screen) rather than against 1.0.
Train on DepMap common-essentiality alone and report how much of the score that single feature already explains.
Measure nearest-neighbour sequence identity between each test gene and the training set and confirm performance does not spike for close neighbours.
leakage_plan.verdict: Leakage is manageable and the fixes are standard; the real hazard here is not leakage but the low measured noise ceiling, which caps any honest result.

success_criteria.metric: Spearman correlation between predicted and measured gene-level log fold change on held-out gene-identity clusters, plus precision among the top 100 predicted tumour-enriched genes, because a lab would take roughly the top 100 into validation.
success_criteria.baselines: Global mean (Spearman 0 by construction); a one-feature DepMap mean-gene-effect baseline; GenePert refit on this label. The paper publishes no predictive number, so there is no published score on this split to beat.
success_criteria.success: Spearman >= 0.30 on held-out gene clusters for the Tumor-vs-Input label, which is close to the measured split-half Spearman ceiling of 0.315, while beating the DepMap-only baseline by at least 0.05; and at least 3 of the 5 paper-named positive controls in the top 200.
success_criteria.kill: Stop if Tumor-vs-Spleen split-half reliability comes out below 0.15 (making the tumour-specific label noise), or if after one week the model is under 0.05 Spearman better than the DepMap-essentiality-only baseline.

ambitious.why: Publishes biology-first machine learning on perturbation data; would need a model that predicts tumour-context-specific T-cell fitness above the measured noise ceiling and nominates edits someone then validates.

realistic.why: Publishes benchmark and evaluation notes; a measured noise ceiling for in vivo T-cell CRISPR screens plus an honest culture-dish-to-tumour transfer evaluation is exactly that size of result.

fallback.why: Takes negative and partial results; the finding that effector-sorted in vivo screen gene scores are only ~10% reliable is publishable even if no model works.

pitch.headline: Four genome-wide CRISPR readouts across 19,113 human genes measured inside live solid tumours, with per-gene reliability I measured directly from the files.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Knockout effects in primary human T cells inside tumours, not cell culture: 19,113 genes, 154,882 guide rows, 8 guides per gene and 2,000 non-targeting control guides, which is enough structure to compute a real noise ceiling.
pitch.the_win: Spearman 0.30 or better on held-out gene families for tumour-infiltration effect, against the measured split-half ceiling of 0.315, while beating a DepMap-essentiality-only baseline by 0.05.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We publish a measured noise ceiling for in vivo T-cell screens: effector-sorted gene scores are about 10% reliable (split-half Pearson 0.051), which tells the field how many guides and mice future screens actually need.
pitch.who_wants_it: The Marson and Carnevale labs at UCSF and Gladstone who ran this screen, plus CAR-T engineering groups deciding which handful of knockouts to put into mice next.

ml_idea: Predict each gene's in vivo T-cell fitness effect in a solid tumour (MAGeCK log2 fold change, Tumor-vs-Input and Tumor-vs-Spleen) from frozen ESM-2 protein embeddings plus DepMap essentiality and public in vitro human T-cell screen features, evaluated on held-out gene-identity clusters against the split-half noise ceiling I measured (Spearman 0.315). The headline question is a transfer question that is informative either way: how much of an in vivo tumour knockout effect is already written in culture-dish and cell-line screens, and what residual is tumour-microenvironment-specific?

effort.compute_note: Parsing the spreadsheets and running the split-half reliability analysis took under two minutes on this laptop (timed). Embedding time is an estimate: 19,113 human proteins through ESM-2 650M at roughly 0.7 sequences per second on CPU; not measured.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Compute split-half reliability of the Tumor-vs-Spleen gene summary (sheets 5-6 of Supplementary Table 1). I already did this for Tumor-vs-Input (Pearson 0.465) and the IFN-gamma effector screen (Pearson 0.051); if Tumor-vs-Spleen falls below ~0.15, the tumour-specific label is noise and the project is dead.

verdict_reason: Part A passes cleanly and the data is genuinely open, tabular and laptop-sized: 19,113 genes x 4 genome-wide comparisons, labels already in a column, 2,000 built-in non-targeting controls, and ESM-2 fits the data type perfectly. But I measured the thing that decides the project and it is bad news on the interesting half. The IFN-gamma effector screen, which is the paper's novel readout, has a gene-level split-half reliability of Pearson 0.051 (Spearman-Brown ~0.10), so roughly 90% of that label is noise and no model can predict it. The one reliable label, Tumor-vs-Input (Pearson 0.465), is dominated by generic cell fitness, which is exactly what DepMap and essentiality predictors already cover. The genuinely novel label, Tumor-vs-Spleen, is a difference of two noisy quantities and I could not verify its reliability because that sheet sits past the 50 MB download cap. Part B also falls short at 7/12 (guides duplicated 2x, no in-file column legend, data split across a 95 MB zip). Park rather than reject: the noise-ceiling measurement is itself a shareable result, and the dataset becomes attractive if folded into a multi-screen human T-cell compendium where in vitro-to-in vivo transfer can be tested properly. Revisit after running the Tumor-vs-Spleen reliability check.
